facts.fact: 醒来时快八点——手机插着电，旁边是 Advil 与半杯水。
facts.anchor: A quick glance at my phone—plugged in on my nightstand, next to a strip of Advil and a half-full glass of water—says it’s almost eight.

facts.fact: 她对 Ruth 说没东西吃、航班今晚起飞、冰箱昨天清空。
facts.anchor: I don’t think I have any food. My flight leaves tonight. I emptied out my fridge yesterday.

facts.fact: Ruth 带来早餐材料并说「我带了早餐」。
facts.anchor: I brought breakfast with us. Everett says you’re an eggs for breakfast girl?

facts.fact: 与父母待一小时后去机场，空客起飞时她无声地哭。
facts.anchor: We spend an hour with Mom and Dad before hitting the road for the airport, and I cry silently as the Airbus takes off into the Texas sunset.

facts.fact: 落地拉瓜迪亚后公交系统混乱——三趟公交两趟地铁才到家。
facts.anchor: I landed into LaGuardia airport as the heavens opened, and thanks to some kind of public transit meltdown, it took three buses and two different subway trains to get home.

facts.fact: 第一支药含贝类衍生物，医生没看出来——立刻过敏。
facts.anchor: because the first medicine I tried contained shellfish derivatives that my doctor didn’t notice, and—naturally—I had an immediate allergic reaction.

facts.fact: 两个月前她飞回德州、毫无预警倒进 Brooks 怀里。
facts.anchor: Two months ago, I flew home to Texas and without even trying—without any warning at all from my beat-up, just-barely-healing heart—fell into the arms of the one man who knows me better than anyone else.

facts.fact: 两人相爱两个月后亲手打破这段关系。
facts.anchor: We had two perfect months of falling all the way in, of building something beautiful. And then between us, we broke it.
